targetReport.title: Territorial Formula Financing
targetReport.description: The federal unconditional transfer to Yukon, the Northwest Territories and Nunavut that closes the gap between what a territory could raise on its own and what it needs to provide services comparable to those in the provinces, calculated under Part I.1 of the Federal-Provincial Fiscal Arrangements Act and Part 1.1 of SOR/2007-303. The fourth major federal transfer alongside the Canada Health Transfer, the Canada Social Transfer and Equalization, and until this entry the only one of the four with no node in this graph. Its revenue-base formula at s. 19 mirrors the DIVISION 2 Nova Scotia formula at s. 8 term for term in several places (SEPH, the System of Macroeconomic Accounts wage terms, Government Finance Statistics), which is what made this pass cheap once the equalization-named-products cluster had already verified the parallel citations.
targetReport.cadence_note: Entitlements are announced in December for the fiscal year beginning the following April 1, alongside Equalization, from the same certificate process.

entries.covers: TFF entitlements for fiscal year 2027-28 (beginning April 1, 2027)

release_schedule.rule: Federal-Provincial Fiscal Arrangements Act (R.S.C. 1985, c. F-8), s. 4.3: "The territorial formula financing payment payable to a territory for a fiscal year shall be calculated, at a time determined by the Minister, no later than three months before that fiscal year begins."
release_schedule.note: Statutory deadline is 3 months before the fiscal year starts (i.e., no later than Dec 31), but in practice Finance Canada has announced TFF and Equalization entitlements earlier in December each year via a joint news release: FY2022-23 announced Dec 16, 2021; FY2023-24 announced Dec 2022; FY2024-25 announced Dec 2023; FY2025-26 announced Dec 23, 2024. The next occurrence (for FY2027-28) is therefore expected around mid-to-late December 2026, with Dec 31, 2026 as the hard statutory backstop.
